notes: Governing check: shear rupture of the two L4x3-1/2x3/8 A36 angles, phiRn = 0.75 x 0.6 x 58 x 6.00 in2 = 156.6 kip against Vu = 142.9 kip (0.912). The net area uses 1.0 in holes for 7/8 in bolts (AISC 360-22 B4.3b). The next closest checks are: outstanding-leg block shear 158.5 kip (0.90), beam-leg block shear 160.2 kip (0.89), beam-side bolts limited by W24x55 web bearing 161.7 kip (0.88), support-side bolts 186.5 kip (0.77), and angle shear yield 194.4 kip (0.73). Beam web shear yield (0.57) and rupture (0.63) and column web bearing (0.47) have wide margins. Spacing, edge distance (J3.4 minimum 1-1/8 in, with the beam edge taken less the 1/4 in underrun) and the 24t and 12t maxima are all met. Each angle is 12 in long, at least T/2 = 10.4 in and within the beam's T. Its top is 2.0 in below the beam top, clear of the 1-7/16 in fillet. Tightening clearance from the bolt to the other leg of the angle is 1.63 in on the beam leg and 2.18 in on the outstanding leg. Assumptions: (1) the W14x61 is a column, and the uncoped W24x55 frames between its flanges. The beam's 7.01 in flange and the angles' 8.4 in width over the outstanding legs both fit inside the column's T = 10-7/8 in. Because the W24x55 is deeper than the W14x61, it cannot frame into a W14x61 girder without heavy copes, which this design does not cover. (2) As in AISC Manual Table 10-1 and Design Example II.A-1, eccentricity is neglected for an all-bolted double angle. (3) The bolts are snug-tight in standard holes, and a 1/2 in setback is assumed. 3/4 in bolts were rejected because four rows bearing on the 0.395 in beam web give only 138.6 kip.
